A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FastAvatar and retain matching core sections and experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 includes readable Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction-quality and runtime measurements in Table 1, loss ablations in Table 2, and qualitative reconstruction experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, expanded component ablations, landmark-perturbation measurements, and long-sequence and streaming reconstruction outcomes in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v2 adds Gaussian importance scores, differentiable Gumbel-Softmax pruning and mask regularization, and reweights the existing losses. It also introduces FramePack-style token compression for long inputs and a streaming procedure using 16-frame windows with four-frame overlap (Section 4.5, Appendices C.3 and D). These extend the retained LGRT architecture and its training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: NeRSemble training and Ava256 evaluation remain. v2 adds INSTA evaluation, explicit testing beyond the training camera viewpoints, and reconstruction under streaming arrival of observations (Figures 7, 11–13). These broaden the evaluated data and observation conditions; additional frame counts alone are not treated as new task coverage.

E2.justification: Figures 7–8 add evaluated comparisons with Arc2Avatar and SynShot on INSTA, and Arc2Avatar and HeadGap on NeRSemble, alongside LAM. The earlier main comparator set and Ava256 comparisons remain. LAM* corresponds to v1's already modified multi-frame LAM renderer rather than an additional comparator.

E3.justification: Reported training changes from 124K iterations with a constant learning rate to 150K with cosine scheduling, and sampled input subsets change from 2–16 to 1–16 frames. v2 adds ArcFace-based identity and Gaussian-count metrics, separates ablations across four input counts, and introduces landmark-perturbation and long-sequence evaluation protocols. These are explicit setting changes and new protocols.

E4.justification: Table 2 expands the two-loss ablation into tests of sliced fusion loss, tracking loss, global attention, Gaussian fusion and pruning across multiple input counts. v2 also adds controlled landmark perturbations (Table 4), frame-packing comparisons (Figure 5), wider-viewpoint tests and concrete failure cases (Figures 10, 12–13), substantially extending analysis of mechanisms and robustness.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 4 includes error bars on its PSNR-versus-input-count curve, although their statistical meaning is unspecified. That curve is removed in v2, whose new long-sequence plot has no uncertainty bars. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces many values: FastAvatar's one-frame PSNR changes from 25.24 to 20.08, and its 16-frame rendering speed from 53 to 17.65 FPS. Revised model and training settings prevent a controlled performance comparison between versions. LAM's one-to-16-frame PSNR trend changes from 17.30–19.42 to 17.30–16.49. v2 also adds identity scores, expanded ablation results, perturbation measurements and long-sequence/streaming outcomes.

T1.justification: v2 extends the Gaussian representation with an importance score, defines binary pruning masks and an L1 mask regularizer, and adds that regularizer to Equation 10. These are limited additions to the mathematical formulation; the existing reconstruction equations remain, and neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: unified feedforward avatar reconstruction from variable-length observations, incremental quality improvement, and a favorable quality–speed trade-off. The added methods and experiments support these existing claims. Removing 'High-Fidelity' from the title does not remove the retained high-quality reconstruction claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of pruning, complementary information from compressed frames and tolerance to FLAME tracking errors. Appendix D explicitly connects failures in wrinkles, gaze and tongue reconstruction to LBS and FLAME topology. Conversely, v1's discussion of tracking-head instability, weak tracking-metric gains and anisotropic-fusion limitations is omitted, substantially changing the account of mechanisms and limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents 521 clips sampled at 15 FPS, camera filtering, background processing, image/token dimensions, attention depth and compression implementation. Reported training duration changes from 12 to 14 days; v1's explicit 10,000-step ablation budget is omitted. Access disclosures also change: v1 advertises code, while v2 advertises code and models but elsewhere promises code after acceptance, leaving availability internally inconsistent.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens cited research to identity-preserving avatars, additional human-avatar methods and feedforward reconstruction. It explicitly grounds new components in LP-3DGS, MaskGaussian and FramePack, and discusses identity-focused work corresponding to the added comparators. These additions extend research positioning beyond the change from numerical to author-year citations; the original VGGT/LAM relationship remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the introduction and methodology wording remain. Changes include title and author-information edits, terminology and citation-style revisions, targeted rewrites of experimental discussions, and relocation of training details into newly organized appendices. The revision does not extensively rewrite the retained narrative.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. The teaser and qualitative comparison grids are redesigned; the Ava256 and ablation displays are revised and renumbered. Table 1 gains an identity column and reorganized input-count blocks, Table 2 expands substantially, and new implementation, robustness, long-sequence, viewpoint and failure-case displays are added. v1's error-bar plot is removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens assessment of the central incremental-reconstruction mechanism: Table 2 isolates additional components across input counts, Table 4 tests dependence on tracking accuracy, and Figures 5 and 11 demonstrate long and streaming inputs. Implementation disclosures and concrete failure cases address v1's limited reproducibility information and narrow validation. Removing unexplained error bars, omitting the ablation budget and giving conflicting code-release statements weaken reporting, but the targeted evidence and technical detail provide a substantial net quality improvement.
